headline: Typical Vaughan home prices are about 5% lower than a year ago, and the Bank of Canada raised its rate in October. New condo sales across the GTA are picking up from a very low base, but few new projects are being sold. In the VMC, 89 development applications are active, so a lot is planned even though building starts are slow.

status.label: Fewer homes under construction
status.explanation: Vaughan had 3,144 homes under construction in September 2026, down from 3,588 a year earlier. Pre-construction condo sales across the GTA fell 61% from a year ago to just 60 units, so fewer new projects are lining up.

status.label: Rebounding from a low base
status.explanation: Vaughan had 263 resale sales in October 2026 and about 4.8 months of inventory, which is a balanced market. GTA new condo sales doubled from a year ago to 760 units, but that is still a small number.

status.label: Prices below last year
status.explanation: The typical Vaughan home cost $1,106,600 in October 2026, down 5.5% from a year ago. A typical condo apartment cost $504,900, down 6.5%. These are Vaughan-wide numbers, not just the VMC.

status.label: Rents flat, vacancy 2.4%
status.explanation: Average rent in the wider Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 a month in 2025, down from $1,762 in 2024. The vacancy rate was 2.4%. This zone is bigger than the VMC.

status.label: Many plans, few starts
status.explanation: Active applications could add about 17,363 homes, but Vaughan housing starts so far in 2026 are 1,243. Higher borrowing costs may slow projects: the policy rate rose to 2.5% on October 28, 2026.

personas.bottom_line: Prices are lower than a year ago, but borrowing costs just moved up.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment cost $504,900 in October 2026, which is 6.5% less than a year earlier.

The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% on October 28, 2026. Posted 5-year mortgage rates were 6.19% in November, up from 6.09% a year ago. Posted rates are higher than most people actually pay.

watch: Bank of Canada decision on December 9, 2026

personas.bottom_line: Rents in the wider area have been flat to slightly lower, with some room to choose.

points.text: Average rent in the Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, compared with $1,762 in 2024. The Toronto-wide average was $1,917.
The vacancy rate in this zone was 2.4% in 2025. A higher rate gives renters more choice.

personas.bottom_line: Larger homes cost less than a year ago, but a rate rise can offset some of that.

points.text: A typical Vaughan townhouse cost $714,500 in October 2026, down 8.9% from a year ago. A typical detached home cost $1,482,000, down 5.4%.

personas.bottom_line: Prices are below last year, and homes are selling near asking price.

points.text: Vaughan homes sold for about 97% of the listing price in October 2026, with about 4.8 months of inventory.
The typical Vaughan home is worth about 30% less than its March 2022 peak of $1,587,400.

personas.bottom_line: Condo prices are lower, but rents are flat and a lot of new supply is planned.

points.text: Completed but unsold new condos in the GTHA were 5,127 units in Q3 2026, near a record. That can limit price growth.
Rents in the wider zone fell from $1,762 to $1,726 between 2024 and 2025, so rental income growth has stalled.
Vaughan completions were 6,368 homes in 2025, a high number. Starts have since dropped, which could tighten supply later.

personas.bottom_line: Condos are cheaper than a year ago, but houses have also fallen, so the gap has not widened.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment cost $504,900 and a typical detached home cost $1,482,000 in October 2026.
Vaughan had 419 condo apartments listed for sale and 57 sold in October 2026. That is a lot of choice for buyers.

scenarios.name: optimistic
scenarios.summary: Demand picks up as sales rebound, supply stays tight, and prices stabilize.

assumptions.assumption: Stays at or near 2.5% through 2027 with no further increases after the October 28, 2026 rise.
Quarterly sales stay at or above the 760 units seen in Q3 2026.

drivers.text: New condo sales doubled from a year ago in Q3 2026.
York Region's 2026 development charges are 2% to 9% lower for residential development, which lowers costs for builders.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.summary: Prices drift sideways to slightly lower, building starts stay low, and the many planned projects move slowly.

assumptions.assumption: Held near 2.5% at the December 9, 2026 decision and the next few decisions.
Stays between about $985,000 and $1,195,000 in April 2027, per the baseline range.

drivers.text: Pre-construction sales fell 61% to just 60 units, so new projects may be slow to start.
89 active applications in the VMC could add about 17,363 homes over time.

scenarios.name: pessimistic
scenarios.summary: Higher rates and high unsold inventory push prices lower and delay projects.

assumptions.assumption: Rises above 2.5% in 2027 if inflation stays high, as the Bank said it was worried about energy prices.
Completed and unsold GTHA inventory stays above 5,000 units.
Falls toward the low end of the baseline range, around $400,000 to $470,000, by late 2027.

drivers.text: A rate increase raises mortgage costs for buyers and borrowing costs for builders.
Units under construction in Vaughan fell from 3,588 to 3,144 in a year.

baseline_views.reason: Prices are 5.5% below last year and the rate rise adds some downside, but sales are recovering. No strong reason to depart from the baseline.
Too far ahead to differ from the baseline; the rate rise and recovering sales roughly balance.
Condo prices are down 6.5% on the year and unsold inventory is high, but sales doubled in Q3.
Large unsold inventory limits gains, while rebounding sales limit falls.
Starts are low, with 1,243 so far in 2026. No cited evidence points to a clear rise or fall.
Pre-construction condo sales fell 61% to 60 units in Q3, which suggests few new apartment projects will start soon.
Units under construction fell from 3,588 to 3,144 in a year and starts are low, so the count is more likely to keep falling.
Rents were flat to slightly lower in 2025 and the vacancy rate was 2.4%.

Region-wide DC rates decrease between 2% and 9% for residential development
